page: Microsoft Azure E96-48ds_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the EDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, with 24 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The server is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory allocation of 14.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 3686 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory performance, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 261.74 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 130.97 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark database operations also demonstrate top-tier performance. However, CPU-bound tasks like single-core stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core perform in the average range. Large-scale LLM text generation on a 70B model is a notable bottleneck, yielding a poor result of 2.41 tokens/sec due to the lack of hardware acceleration.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local SSD storage, this server offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound and storage-heavy workloads. It is highly suitable for large relational databases, in-memory caching, data analytics, and high-throughput static web serving. It is less optimal for GPU-dependent deep learning or compute-heavy tasks that do not leverage its massive memory footprint.
